inline_comments.comment:
RST section-level bug. In RST, heading levels are assigned by the order each underline character is first encountered. Because `...` (dots) appears first here, it becomes the first sub-level, and all later `---` sections ('Basic controls', 'Plotting data from the command line', 'Configuring the GUI', 'Polling the GUI') will be rendered as *sub-sections* of 'Selecting a part of a trajectory' rather than as siblings. Fix by using `---` (dashes) consistently for all top-level sections on this page:

```rst
Selecting a part of a trajectory
---------------------------------
```
Grammatical error: "These constraints will be then be saved to a file" contains a duplicated 'be'. Should read "These constraints will then be saved to a file".
Grammar error: "Depending on you operating system" should be "Depending on your operating system".

The attention block text "This functionality is currently disabled" is missing a terminal period. Additionally, line 6 contains trailing whitespace (four spaces on an otherwise blank line inside the directive body), which most linters will flag.
Trailing whitespace at the end of the line after "create the". The line reads `...can be used to create the ` (note the space before the newline). Remove the trailing space.

The two lines

```rst
.. ::

..   $ ase gui --interpolate 3 initial.xyz final.xyz -o interpolated_path.traj
```

are RST comments that silently hide content. The intent is unclear — if this NEB interpolation workflow is worth documenting, it should be rendered as a proper code block; if it is genuinely obsolete or out of scope, these lines should simply be deleted rather than left as invisible commented-out noise.

Lines 24–26 comment out a useful `repeat` parameter example:

```rst
.. or

.. >>> view(atoms, repeat=(3, 3, 2))
```

Since this is hidden via RST comment syntax, readers never see it. Either include it as a rendered alternative (e.g., with a brief explanatory sentence) or remove the dead comment lines entirely.

This line uses `:ref:\`ase-gui\`` to link to the GUI page, whose title was changed from "ASE's GUI" to "Graphical user interface" in this same MR. Sphinx will now render the sentence as "the Graphical user interface automatically displays certain information", which is grammatically awkward. Consider replacing the ref with plain text, e.g. "the GUI automatically displays certain information", or restructuring the sentence.

The 'Show labels' bullet list does not match the updated menu labels in `gui.py`. After this MR the menu choices are (from `gui.py`): 'Atom index', 'Magnetic moments' (plural), 'Element symbol', 'Initial charges' (plural). The docs list 'Magnetic moment' (singular), 'Chemical symbol' (rather than 'Element symbol'), and 'Initial charge' (singular). Align the documentation bullet text with the actual menu strings so users can find the options by name.

general_comments.comment: The 'Writing files' section (including the `-o` flag example and the list of supported output formats — `traj`, `xyz`, `cube`, `pdb`, `eps`, `png`, `pov`) was removed entirely. While the format list may go stale, the existence of the `-o` flag and the ability to write files from the command line are practical features that new users are likely to look for in a 'basics' guide. Consider either retaining a minimal version of this section (with a pointer to `ase.io` docs for the full format list) or verifying the information is easily discoverable elsewhere.

The sentence-case corrections to menu labels in `gui.py` (e.g., 'Show _Labels' → 'Show _labels', 'Quick Info' → 'Quick info', 'Change View' → 'Change view', 'B_ulk Modulus' → 'B_ulk modulus') are a consistent and welcome tidying of the UI. No issues here.
